description:
FOUND s438e (Opus 5) while measuring #455, and it is the reason #455's repair
is keyed on the FEATURE BOUNDARY and not on the prototype TEXT.

  use strict; use warnings;
  our $a = 123;
  {
      no warnings "illegalproto";
      sub t000 ($a) { $a || "z" }
      print &t000(456), "\n";      # perl: 123      PCL: 456
  }
  use feature "signatures";

perl reads `($a)` as an old-style PROTOTYPE here (the feature is not enabled at
that point) and an illegal one, which it IGNORES -- so the body's `$a` is the
package `our $a`, and `&t000(456)` (the `&` form ignores the prototype anyway)
returns 123.  This is perl-tests/signatures.t lines 17-20, asserting it
directly, and the row is BLESSED in docs/fail-baseline.tsv:

  signatures.t  1  ($a) not signature when not enabled  '456'  '123'

MECHANISM, and it is NOT the signature/prototype routing: PCL takes the
old-prototype path for this sub (verified -- the emission is
`(p-sub pl-t000 ($a) (block nil â¦ (p-|| $a "z")))`), and that path puts the
prototype's NAMES straight into the CL lambda list.  So the name is bound as a
parameter on BOTH paths, and choosing between them cannot fix it.  #455 leaves
the emission of this file byte-identical (corpus-diff over the 111) precisely
because it only moves the boundary case.

FIX SHAPE: an old-style prototype never binds parameters (Parser2's
`_is_pure_prototype` says so in its own comment: "A PURE old-style prototype
never binds parameters -- the body is a plain @_-consuming body").  The gap is
that a prototype carrying identifier characters is not "pure" by that textual
test, yet perl treats it as a prototype all the same when the feature is off.
So the lowering needs the same three-way answer the head reader now has:
signature (feature on, named params) -> bind; prototype (feature off) -> do NOT
bind, whatever the text looks like; pure prototype -> do not bind.
`Pl::Parser::_signatures_enabled_at` (added by #455) is the predicate.

BAR: the signatures.t row leaves docs/fail-baseline.tsv by EDIT; a row in
Pl/t/sig-param-shadow-01.t (which documents this gap in place, deliberately
NOT asserting it today); corpus-diff + the four-population A/B, since this
changes emission for any sub with a named prototype outside a signature region;
full sweep.
subject: SILENT WRONG: an old-style prototype with NAMES (`sub t000 ($a)` where the signatures feature is OFF) binds its names as PARAMETERS -- perl ignores an illegal prototype, so `$a` is the package variable (blessed baseline fail in signatures.t)
